newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end near day's peak, market relaxed.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end near day's peak, market relaxed.

text.p: * Telecom hits all-time high of NZ$7.05
* Wilson & Horton falls close to INP offer price
* Warehouse rebounds sharply after 4-month result
Price movements at close.
LAST CHG
325 -1 * NZSC cap index -1.87 at 4,410.81
357 -3 * Volume NZ$59 million. Futures +6 at 1,143
705 +10 * Other movers - -13 +24
New Zealand share prices ended strongly but just off their peak on Friday after Telecom hit an all-time high of NZ$7.05. Investors were still appearing relaxed about the upcoming October 12 election.
John Rowley at SBC Warburg said the market seemed to be taking its cue from ratings agency Standard and Poor's, which broadly does not expect a major shift in economic policy after the election.
Those views were echoed by a poll in the National Business Review, which said the business community did not generally expect a major departure from the status quo.

"It's intriguing. We will not know until the Monday after the election whether that's right or not," Rowley said. "Certainly, pre-election, it's hard to see whether there is going to be any great fall-out," he said.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 8.55 points higher at 2,244.28 on turnover worth NZ$59 million, helped along by a 10 cent move up in Telecom to a record high of $7.05.
But Rowley said it was a discerning market.
The normally high-performing stocks like Air New Zealand, which has the task of bedding down a large capital raising, were struggling a little.
The Warehouse was re-rated by 24 cents to NZ$2.85 after releasing a result for the first four months, indicating the business is back to a manageable situation.

Wilson and Horton eased 13 cents to NZ$10.57, but was still seven cents higher than the intended NZ$10.50 offer price of Independent, indicating some may be holding out for a higher level before the bid is formally launched.
On the horizon there was the election to consider.
"But the market seems quite convinced on the election impact so it's hard to see whether there will be much change," Rowley said. -- James Gray (64 9 302 1253)
